Bayes Studio, a Vancouver-based startup, develops AI-driven wildfire detection systems using edge-deployed camera devices. 
Their existing workflow consists of manual labeling, model training, and compression. 
This results in inefficiencies to pre-label image data and update models in a timely manner.
This project addresses that bottleneck by developing an automated and modular pipeline for end-to-end model improvement.

The pipeline is designed to process incoming data through a semi-automated labeling system that combines predictions from two models (YOLOv8[@yolov8_ultralytics] and Grounding DINO[@grounding_dino]) with human-in-the-loop validation for uncertain cases. Labeled images then undergo data augmentation to increase dataset diversity. The pipeline fine-tunes a YOLOv8 base model on this new dataset and applies knowledge distillation and quantization to produce smaller, deployable models for edge devices.

Key outputs include a labeled dataset, fine-tuned and compressed models, and versioned metadata to support traceability and reproducibility. While the system currently runs locally, it provides a foundation for scalable wildfire detection workflows. Limitations such as lack of cloud support, de-centralized metadata storage, and missing monitoring tools are acknowledged, with recommendations proposed to address them.

Overall, this solution helps the partner streamline model updates and prepare models suitable for real-time edge deployment in wildfire detection.
